text: I've led this town's herds for close to twenty years.
Ena and I decide together when a pasture has become unsafe to use.
Salt-crust has spread across three pastures that were healthy grazing land in my youth.
It spreads fastest near the Old Canal Bed and near the kilns.
Bran has told me the woodland is thinning in roughly the same direction the salt spreads.
I don't think that's a coincidence, though I can't prove a connection.
Kiri notices these changes as fast as I do, and she's barely more than a child.
I give her real responsibility because she's earned it, not because she's convenient.
I was a young herder when the river began its shift. It took years, not one night.
I correct the 'one bad night' story whenever I hear it told to children as fact.
Tarek has heard my salt-crust reports. He calls it a slow problem for a slower season.
I think slow problems are the ones that end towns, not the sudden ones.
The archive-keeper asked me once whether old grazing maps matched current usable land.
They don't. Nearly a third of the old grazing land marked usable then is salt-crusted now.
I've shifted the herds' whole seasonal rotation to compensate, without formal approval.
